start.finding: The 47-case browser candidate had 46 passing cases and one desktop urgency failure: the matter toolbar and dialog were both absent while the main app, saved matter and later upload controller existed. Static script requests were logged, but response bodies/statuses, request failures and console errors were not; no lower transport cause can be established from those artifacts.

recheck.meaning: An unchanged recheck passed; it neither identifies nor fixes the original transport cause.

start.artifact_limit: The original XML is retained. The diagnostic JSON, HTML and PNG at the same test-derived paths were overwritten by the recheck; this record does not claim their original bytes are preserved.
start.contract: Record local static response status, body length and SHA256 outside event callbacks; callbacks retain only response references or cached metadata. Guard real goto/reload against missing, unsuccessful or empty required assets derived from the current document's script/stylesheet manifest before workflow assertions. Preserve all existing test assertions and populations.
start.scope: Shared synthetic browser fixture diagnostic and its fail-closed coverage check only. No production transport fix, file retry, new failure allowance or urgency assertion change.

build.changes: The shared fixture observes local static responses and failed requests/console errors, hashes response bodies only outside callbacks, and guards goto/reload against missing, unsuccessful or empty document-required scripts/styles before workflow assertions. No original workflow assertion was changed.
build.negative_controls: Three separate parameterized browser controls plant HTTP503 with a body, HTTP200 with an empty body, or an aborted response for a script confirmed in the actual served document. Each requires exactly one intercepted request, the navigation guard's refusal naming that required asset, and matching response/hash or failure diagnostics. These three controls are not counted as successful user journeys.
build.static_check: Ruff checked both changed Python files: all checks passed. No pytest, browser or gate execution was performed by this author.

central_diagnostic.result: One workflow passed; teardown raised KeyError removing the same held-response listener twice. The added independent asset observer kept the response event alive and exposed a pre-existing subscription-ownership defect. The initial expanded run was interrupted after repeated teardown errors and is not a complete result.
central_diagnostic.repair: HeldReply now owns an explicit listening flag and one idempotent unsubscribe method used by release and abandon. It does not remove other observers or swallow exceptions; every user-flow assertion is unchanged.

test.next: Coordinator runs the existing 47-case browser population plus the three new delivery controls after source freeze; report user journeys and negative controls separately.

completion: The original transport cause remains unresolved. Better observation and prevention of unobserved asset coverage is not a claim to have repaired that cause, completed BK-41 or earned release approval.
